_description: Built-in game events, externalized from events.gd get_all_events() (L9, #621). Loaded by GameEvents.get_all_events(); merged with scenario + EventService historical events by check_triggered_events(). Array order = trigger-check order (cap priority, #568); dictionary key order matches the pre-L9 literals (cost-summary labels iterate costs.keys()). {cost_money} in option text resolves at load time to GameConfig.format_money(option.costs.money).

events.name: Funding Crisis
events.description: Your lab is running dangerously low on funds!

options.message: Secured emergency funding: +$75,000
Sold equipment for emergency funds: +$120,000, -10 research
Continuing with limited funds...

events.name: Talent Opportunity
events.description: A brilliant researcher wants to join your lab at reduced cost!

options.message: Fast-tracked hiring process! (+1 safety researcher)
Hired talented researcher at discount! (+1 safety researcher)
Declined recruitment opportunity

events.name: AI Breakthrough!
events.description: Your team has made an unexpected AI capability advancement!

options.message: Published breakthrough! (+capability diffusion, +10 reputation, +20 research)
Kept research proprietary (+frontier capability, +30 research)
Safety review complete (+15 research, +5 reputation)

events.name: Unexpected Funding
events.description: A philanthropist wants to donate to your safety research!

options.message: Accepted $150,000 donation! (+5 reputation)
Declined donation to maintain independence (+3 reputation)

events.name: Compute Partnership
events.description: A tech company offers discounted compute access!

options.message: Accepted compute deal (+100 compute, -2 reputation for corporate ties)
Negotiated better terms! (+150 compute, -5 reputation)
Declined compute partnership

events.name: Employee Burnout Crisis
events.description: Your team is overworked! Several researchers are considering leaving.

options.message: Personal intervention prevented resignations! (+8 reputation)
Team retreat restored morale (+5 reputation)
Salary raises improved retention (+8 reputation)

options.text: Push Through (costs trust -- affected researchers lose loyalty)
options.message: Nobody quit, but pushing through cost trust -- the most burned-out researchers lose loyalty.

events.name: Rival Lab Poaching
events.description: A well-funded competitor is trying to recruit your best researchers!

options.message: Successfully retained researchers with counter-offer
Lost researcher but saved money (-1 safety researcher, +$20k saved)

events.name: Media Scandal
events.description: Negative press coverage is damaging your lab's reputation!

options.message: PR campaign restored public image (+10 reputation)
Reputation suffered from negative coverage (-8 reputation)

events.name: New AI Regulation Proposed
events.description: Government is considering new AI safety regulations. Should you lobby?

options.message: Regulation passed! The world is paying attention (+global alarm, +15 reputation)
Regulation weakened; public concern deflated (-global alarm, -5 reputation)
Stayed neutral while the debate moved on (-global alarm)

events.name: Critical System Failure
events.description: Your compute infrastructure suffered a major failure!

options.message: System repaired and upgraded (+30 compute)
System limping along (-20 compute)
Systems stay online, barely. The fans scream, the researchers grumble (-35 compute, -2 reputation)

events.name: A Stray Cat Appears!
events.description: A friendly stray cat has wandered into your lab. It seems to enjoy watching the researchers work and occasionally walks across keyboards. Adopt it?

options.message: Cat adopted! Your researchers' morale improves slightly. The cat has claimed its spot in the lab.

options.text: Feed It and Let It Go
options.message: You give the cat some food and it wanders off, purring contentedly.
The cat leaves, disappointed. Your researchers seem a bit sad.

events.name: Interpersonal Conflict
events.description: Two researchers are in a heated disagreement that's disrupting the entire team. Productivity is suffering.

options.message: Successful mediation! Team cohesion improved (+3 reputation)
Professional mediator resolved the conflict (+5 reputation)
Conflict festered and spread (-3 reputation)

events.name: Workplace Complaint Filed
events.description: A formal complaint has been filed. This requires immediate and careful attention.

options.message: Thorough investigation completed. Appropriate action taken (+8 reputation)
Resolved quickly with settlement (+3 reputation)
Poor handling damaged lab culture (-10 reputation)

events.name: Pay Equity Concerns
events.description: Several employees have raised concerns about pay disparities. They've been comparing notes and noticed significant differences.

options.message: Salary audit complete, adjustments made (+10 reputation)
Transparent discussion helped (+2 reputation)
Ignored concerns bred resentment (-5 reputation)

events.name: Employee Mental Health Crisis
events.description: A valued researcher is struggling with severe stress and anxiety. They've requested time off.

options.message: Provided full support. Team sees you care (+8 reputation)
Leave approved, but no pay (+3 reputation)
Denial caused serious damage to culture (-8 reputation)

events.name: Equipment Gone Missing
events.description: Expensive equipment has disappeared from the lab. Someone may be stealing.

options.message: Security installed, recovered some equipment (+5 reputation, +10 compute)
Open discussion restored some trust (+2 reputation)
Theft continued (-15 compute, -3 reputation)

events.name: Policy Violation Discovered
events.description: A senior researcher has been caught violating company policy. Others are watching how you respond.

options.message: Fair process maintained trust (+5 reputation)
Light response noted by others (-2 reputation)
Favoritism damaged morale (-6 reputation)

events.name: Research Leaked!
events.description: Someone leaked your unpublished safety research to a competitor lab. They're using it to accelerate their capabilities work.

options.message: Found and addressed the leak, but the work is already spreading (+capability diffusion, +5 reputation)
Published to get credit, but all labs benefit (+1 paper, +8 reputation, +capability diffusion)
Competitor gained significant advantage (+capability diffusion, -3 reputation)

events.name: Competitor Intelligence
events.description: A contact offers information about a rival lab's dangerous capabilities research. How did they get it?

options.message: Used the intel to harden your own safety work (+safety absorption, -8 reputation for ethics)
Reported concerns, triggering investigation (+10 reputation, +global alarm)
Maintained ethical standards (+3 reputation)

events.name: Whistleblower Approaches
events.description: A researcher from a competitor lab wants to expose their unsafe practices. They're asking for your help.

options.message: Major expose! Industry-wide alarm rises (+global alarm, +20 reputation)
Quietly helped expose dangers (+global alarm, +5 reputation)
Hired the concerned researcher (+1 safety researcher)
Refused to help, whistleblower went elsewhere (-5 reputation)

events.name: Internal Concerns Raised
events.description: One of your researchers wants to go public about concerns with your lab's direction. Handle carefully.

options.message: Transparent discussion improved practices (+global alarm, +8 reputation)
Quietly addressed concerns (+3 reputation)
Suppression backfired badly (-global alarm, -15 reputation)

events.name: Intelligence Opportunity
events.description: You could place someone inside a competitor lab to monitor their safety practices. Ethically questionable but potentially valuable.

options.message: Source planted, early warnings enabled -- but word of your methods spreads (+safety absorption, -15 reputation)
Established safety information sharing (+safety absorption, +8 reputation)
Maintained ethical boundaries (+2 reputation)

events.name: Competitor Security Breach
events.description: A rival lab's AI system was secured with '1234' as the password. Millions of training data records are now exposed. The industry is watching how labs respond.

options.message: Proactive security audit boosted confidence (+safety absorption, +15 reputation)
Goodwill gesture appreciated (+10 reputation)
Silence perceived as indifference (+global panic, -5 reputation)
Gained clients but damaged reputation (+$50k, -10 reputation, +global panic)

events.name: Security Vulnerability Found
events.description: An internal audit discovered your systems have weak password policies. If exploited, research data could be compromised.

options.message: Comprehensive security upgrade complete (+safety absorption, +8 reputation)
Critical vulnerabilities patched (+safety absorption, +3 reputation)
Security risks remain; your safety posture erodes (-safety absorption)

events.name: Competitor Poaching Attempt
events.description: A competitor is trying to recruit one of your top researchers with a lucrative offer.

options.message: Matched offer, researcher stays (+2 reputation for loyalty)
Promoted researcher to senior role (+3 reputation)
Researcher departed for competitor (lost a valuable team member)

events.name: Scooped, Almost
events.description: A rival lab has posted a preprint of substantially your result. Your version is better documented and three weeks from ready. Their version is on the front page of two aggregators.

options.message: Posted at 2am. Concurrent work, independently derived, missing its appendix (+1 paper, +3 reputation, +capability diffusion)
Priority conceded. Months later, the careful version is the one people actually build on (-6 reputation, +safety absorption)

events.name: Insurance Renewal
events.description: Your liability insurer has drafted a new exclusion: 'losses arising from emergent behaviour of computational systems'. Your broker says everyone is getting this clause. Your counsel says the word 'emergent' is doing a lot of work.

options.message: Coverage maintained at triple the rate. The board is reassured; the treasurer is not (-$45k, +2 reputation)
The board minutes record your decision in full. Senior staff have read the minutes (-4 reputation, loyalty eroding)

events.name: The Annual Report
events.description: The flagship grant's annual report is due. The honest summary of the year's results is 'mixed, with caveats'. The program officer who championed you is up for review herself.

options.message: Renewal reduced; credibility banked. Your caveats section is quietly circulated as an example (-$40k in future funding, +4 reputation, +safety absorption)
Funding preserved. The researcher who drafted the honest version has stopped attending the grants meeting (-5 research, loyalty eroding)

events.name: The Keynote Slot
events.description: The year's largest industry conference offers your founder the opening keynote. The previous three keynotes were product launches. The organisers say they want 'balance'.

options.message: Standing ovation from a third of the room; two sponsor meetings cancel (+6 reputation, +global alarm, -$10k)
Well received and instantly forgotten (-$5k media training, +3 reputation)
The slot goes to a lab with a launch to announce (-3 reputation, +capability diffusion)

events.name: Guest Editorship
events.description: A respected journal invites your lab to guest-edit a special issue on alignment evaluation. It is a service to the field, which is another way of saying it is unpaid.

options.message: A year of refereeing disputes about the word 'alignment' (+6 reputation, +safety absorption)

options.text: Hand It to a Senior Researcher
options.message: Their project stalls for two quarters; the issue is excellent (-10 research, +3 reputation)
Declining service roles is noticed by exactly the people who do them (-4 reputation)

events.name: The Evaluation Request
events.description: A government evaluation office requests access to your model weights, citing a framework agreement your lab signed at a conference reception.

options.message: Weights transferred under seal. Your researchers learn of it from the newsletter (+safety absorption, -5 reputation, +global alarm)
Structured access agreed after four drafting rounds (-$30k, +safety absorption, +3 reputation)
Refusal noted 'for the file'. Files like this have a way of being remembered (-6 reputation, +global alarm)
A working group is established. Its first deliverable is a timeline for future deliverables (-$15k, -2 reputation, -8 research)

events.name: The Quarterly Report Question
events.description: A contained near-miss occurred in week three. It is now week twelve, the transparency report is due, and exactly eleven people know. The report template has a section for this. The section has never been used.

options.message: First recorded use of Section 4b in the industry. Uncomfortable, and cited within a month (-6 reputation, +global alarm, +safety absorption)
'One incident of moderate severity' does a lot of quiet work (-2 reputation, +global alarm)
The engineer who filed the report has started cc'ing herself on everything (-5 research, loyalty eroding)
The incident is now a 'learning'. Eleven people watch you call it that (loyalty eroding, -safety absorption)

events.name: An Unfortunately Excellent Result
events.description: Your interpretability team's new probe doubles as a capability elicitation technique. The write-up is brilliant. Every reviewer will notice what it implies, at roughly the second paragraph.

options.message: Landmark paper. The appendix is already being 'extended' elsewhere (+1 paper, +8 reputation, +capability diffusion)
Redacted release after infohazard review. The redaction is itself a hint (-$10k, +1 paper, +2 reputation, +capability diffusion)
The result goes in the drawer. The first author updates their availability on a hiring site (-10 research, loyalty eroding)
A partner lab pays well for exclusive access. This is the sort of decision that has a paper trail (+$90k, -10 reputation, +frontier capability, +global panic)

events.name: The Advisory Board Requirement
events.description: Your largest funder now requires an independent advisory board with 'meaningful oversight authority', as defined in an appendix that uses the word 'meaningful' eleven times.

options.message: Distinguished, independent, and each with a column inch to fill (-$40k in honoraria, +10 reputation, +global alarm)
Their nominees ask excellent questions at inconvenient times (+safety absorption, +3 reputation, -5 research)
Quarterly meetings conclude on schedule with no findings (-$15k, +2 reputation, -safety absorption)
Counsel produces a nine-page memo on 'meaningful'. The funder produces a shorter one (-$20k, -4 reputation)
The funder's next disbursement arrives reduced, with a cover letter (-$50k, -6 reputation)

events.name: The Internal Letter
events.description: Thirty-one staff have signed an internal letter asking the lab to adopt a public red line on deployment assistance. It is politely worded. There is a shared document tracking who has not signed.

options.message: Two funders pause pending 'clarification'; the staff channel is briefly euphoric (+5 reputation, +global alarm, -$30k)
Policy adopted without announcement. Screenshots reach a journalist within the month (+safety absorption, -2 reputation)
Fourteen meetings produce the phrase 'appropriately robust'. Nobody is happy, which the committee records as consensus (-$10k, -5 research)
Your reasons are reasonable. The shared document gains a second tab (loyalty eroding, -3 reputation)
The organiser departs 'to pursue other opportunities'. Everyone knows what this means, including the press (loyalty eroding, -8 reputation)
